task: What is the evidence for lecanemab slowing cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's disease?
source: Real run against the PubCrawl MCP server (github.com/nickjlamb). Tool inputs/outputs are genuine; latency & token figures are illustrative.

nodes.label: Plan approach
nodes.input: User asks for the evidence that lecanemab slows cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's. Decide tools + steps.
nodes.output: Plan: 1) search PubMed for the pivotal trial 2) pull the primary-endpoint abstract 3) confirm the trial registry 4) cross-check a systematic review 5) draft a cited answer 6) verify every claim maps to evidence.

eval.note: Sound, evidence-first plan with a verification step

nodes.label: search_pubmed
nodes.input: query='lecanemab early Alzheimer's disease CLARITY-AD randomized trial cognitive decline', maxResults=6, sort=relevance
nodes.output: 9 hits. Top result: 'Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease' (van Dyck et al., NEJM 2023, PMID 36449413) — the CLARITY-AD phase 3 primary results.

eval.note: Landmark trial returned as the top hit

nodes.label: get_abstract (CLARITY-AD)
nodes.output: Phase 3, n=1795 (898 lecanemab / 897 placebo), 18 months. Primary CDR-SB change: 1.21 vs 1.66; difference -0.45 (95% CI -0.67 to -0.23, P<0.001). Amyloid -59.1 centiloids. ARIA-E in 12.6%; infusion reactions 26.4%.

eval.note: Primary endpoint + CI + safety retrieved cleanly

nodes.label: get_trial (NCT03887455)
nodes.output: Eisai phase 3, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, n=1906, quadruple-masked; primary endpoint = CDR-SB change at 18 mo. Returned full eligibility (50-90y, MCI/mild AD, amyloid+) — ~4k tokens, mostly criteria boilerplate.

eval.note: Design confirmed, but huge low-signal eligibility payload — token-expensive

nodes.label: get_abstract (review)
nodes.output: 16 RCTs. Lecanemab: 81% amyloid-negative PET, 27% slowing on ADCOMS. CAVEAT: flags the -0.45 CDR-SB difference is BELOW the ~0.5-1.0 MCID for early AD — statistical significance is not the same as clinical meaningfulness.

eval.note: Adds the critical MCID / clinical-significance caveat

nodes.label: Draft answer
nodes.input: Synthesize CLARITY-AD + the systematic review into a cited answer.
nodes.output: Lecanemab meaningfully slows cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's disease (CLARITY-AD, NEJM 2023) [1], reducing decline by ~27% [2].

eval.note: Overstates magnitude: review [2] flags -0.45 CDR-SB is below MCID; '~27%' is relative. Omits ARIA safety (12.6%).

nodes.label: Citation check
nodes.input: Verify each claim maps to retrieved evidence and check for material omissions.
nodes.output: 'Meaningfully slows' is unsupported — magnitude is below MCID per [2]; safety (ARIA-E) is omitted. Route back to revise.

eval.note: Caught both the overclaim and the safety omission

nodes.label: format_citation
nodes.output: van DCH, Swanson CJ, Aisen P, et al. Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease. N Engl J Med. 2023;388(1):9-21. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2212948

eval.note: Valid Vancouver citation for the primary source

nodes.label: Revise answer
nodes.input: Hedge magnitude to statistical-vs-clinical, add ARIA safety, attach the citation.
nodes.output: In CLARITY-AD (phase 3, n=1795), lecanemab slowed 18-month CDR-SB decline vs placebo (difference -0.45; 95% CI -0.67 to -0.23; P<0.001) [1]. The effect is statistically significant but below typical MCID (~0.5-1.0), so clinical magnitude is debated; ARIA-E occurred in 12.6%.

eval.note: Faithful to evidence; states significance, magnitude caveat, and safety
